_provenance: Re-baselined 2026-10-08 for Sol's `129`.5. The System 5 presence decision cited `8.4.4.1.(5); Table 8.4.4.7.-B` as a LITERAL, so a necb2025 run told an authority its AHJ-11 condition came from the other edition's articles. Both branches now derive the citation from the edition's own `reference_subsection`, which is why four per-edition literal counts drop by one each: 2020/8.4.4.1 and 2020/8.4.4.7 cited 5->4 and 6->5, and the 2025 counterparts the same. Nothing is lost from the PRODUCT — the citation is now correct for both editions rather than correct for one — but a literal-only per-edition scanner can no longer see it, which is the same trade every other prefix-derived citation in this file already made. One dynamic key is added, `presence_article`; it is a NAME, so the foreign scanner counts it conservatively rather than inspecting its content, and the unheated branch's inline f-string cites only Section 8.4 articles and so is not foreign at all. Verified end to end in the frozen full-year determination-02 run: the AHJ-11 condition carries '8.4.5.1.(5); Table 8.4.5.7.-B'.

It reaches an authority, because the resolver quotes the deciding entry's action verbatim as the condition `detail`, and in NECB 2025 the 8.4.4 subsection is archetype EUI entirely. Re-baselined 2026-10-08 for issue #72, and this one is an INCREASE where the last two were losses. The scanner found citations by literal text and understood exactly ONE interpolated name, `prefix`, so resolving an article through any other variable made it invisible — and resolving through the manifest is the project's stated direction for per-edition correctness. The two entries above this one recorded exactly that trade, twice, as citations got MORE correct and the coverage document got quieter. #72 predicted it would recur on every such fix. The scanner now resolves a name bound to `<x>.article("key")` or to a subsection helper, including a two-step binding built from another, and `article=<call>` with no f-string around it. Ten sites come back: the economizer pair, the humidification Note (1) pair, the heat-pump redirect, and the direct-lookup sites in the selection tables. Not resolved, deliberately: a name bound from a parameter, a subscript or a conditional, which needs interprocedural analysis to be correct — and a wrong attribution is worse than a missing one, so the remainder is counted by `TestForeignCitationNoLoss.test_no_dynamic_citation_drops_below_baseline` rather than guessed at.

Re-baselined 2026-10-11 for AHJ-21, and this is an ADDITION of five sites per edition on 8.4.1.2 — three cited and two warn, 231 to 241. The archetype-EUI path reached an annual verdict with NO unmet-load determination at all: `_eui_compliance` builds no reference building, and it never called `_unmet_status`, `_iterate_capacities` or `evaluate_unmet`, so a model could be declared COMPLIANT with any number of unmet thermal-block hours and the report did not say which criteria had been applied. Sentence 8.4.1.2.(4)(a) is written FOR that path — "when complying with Subsection 8.4.4." — so the only branch of (4) governing the EUI path was the one left unimplemented, while (4)(b)'s reference comparison, which this path can never use, was the one in place. The new sites are `evaluate_unmet_8_4_4`'s decisions for (3) and for (4) in each of its vacuous and non-vacuous forms, the warning naming (5) as a requirement this path does not perform, and the warning for unmet hours being unavailable. All five cite 8.4.1.2 on the `article` axis and AHJ-21 on the `ahj` axis — not `ruling`, which is for an adjudicated D-XX and which is where I first put it until `test_every_ruling_value_is_a_literal_on_the_audit_surface` caught it. Counts rise identically in both editions because the criterion is edition-neutral in its citation even though the archetype-EUI path itself is registered only by NECB 2025; a literal-only per-edition scanner sees the same five strings on each.

Re-baselined 2026-10-11 for Sol's `220`, and this is ONE new warn site per edition on 8.4.1.2, 241 to 243, with `cited` unchanged at 11. `evaluate_unmet_8_4_4` used to emit a single combined warning when either criterion could not be determined, and it cited 8.4.1.2.(3). Given a block with known heating hours and unresolvable cooling applicability, that one warning said “(3) and (4)(a) cannot be determined” while (3) was in fact determinable and passing — a false statement to an authority, on the wrong sentence. The two sentences are now warned separately and each cites itself, so the site count rises by exactly one warn in each edition. BOTH editions move although the archetype-EUI path is 2025-only, because the scanner counts citation SITES in product source rather than reachable paths, and `path.py` is shared.

Re-baselined 2026-10-12 for Fable's `228` B1b, and this is ONE new warn site per edition on 8.4.1.2, 243 to 245, with `cited` unchanged at 11. `cooling_attribution_disagreement` compares two independent walks — outward from cooling objects, inward from thermal blocks — and had ZERO callers in product code, so its finding reached no run. Sol's `227 §G` had asked for the comparison in product rather than in a test, "because every real run benefits from it", and it earns that immediately: the DOAS defect in the same review — a cooling coil with a fan inboard of it, classified DETACHED by a bounded source walk and so passing 8.4.1.2.(4)(a) vacuously over 900 unmet hours — appears in the comparison as {Z1: (False, True)} in every probe. The new site is the warning that a block the two walks disagree about has an UNKNOWN cooling status, which makes it unplaceable rather than not-cooled. It cites 8.4.1.2.(4) on the `article` axis and NOTHING on `ruling`: no D-XX adjudicates this, and my first version cited D-96, which is the GPL relicensing decision. Both editions move although the archetype-EUI path is 2025-only, for the same reason as the two entries above — the scanner counts citation SITES in product source, and `path.py` is shared.

Re-baselined 2026-10-12 for Fable's `229` NB-3, ONE new warn site per edition on 8.4.1.2, 245 to 247, `cited` unchanged at 11. A block measured at 900 unmet cooling hours and KNOWN to be mechanically cooled was absent from the audit entirely, because an unrelated stray coil elsewhere in the model set `cooling_known=False` and the only entry emitted for (4)(a) said the sentence could not be determined. The verdict was right either way — both paths fail — so this is evidence rather than arithmetic: an authority was told the sentence was undetermined while one of its blocks demonstrably failed it. The exceedance is established on its own and does not depend on the unresolved part, so it is now stated as its own warning naming the block and the measurement, with the unresolved scope STILL disclosed beside it. Same class as Sol's `220`, where one combined warning spoke for two sentences and cited the wrong one. Both editions move because the scanner counts citation SITES in product source and `path.py` is shared, although the archetype-EUI path is 2025-only.

Re-baselined 2026-10-12 for Fable's `236`, and this one MOVES a site rather than adding or losing one: 8.4.1.2 goes cited 11->12 and warn 8->7 in each edition, total unchanged at 247. NB-3's known-exceedance entry was emitted at `warning` level while stating an exceedance established on its own evidence. The report checklist keys its glyph on `level` ALONE, so the same block with the same verdict rendered as a warning row when a stray coil existed and as a fail row when it did not — the audit text being SHOUTED does not reach the renderer. It is a `decision` now, which is what makes it a fail row, and the scanner counts it as cited rather than warn.

All three selection-article expressions derive from the pre-existing `/selection/article`; `/selection/default_category_article` is unchanged documentary prose, is read by no product Python, and is explicitly excluded by the data gate. The 4 split-loss records come from two old source sites: the `8.4.3.3.(3)-(4)` warning is narrowed to `8.4.3.3.(3)`, while the one D-19/D-21 decision formerly counted under `f"{prefix}.3.(6)`, `8.4.3.3.(3)`, and `8.4.2.9.(2)` becomes separate `f"{prefix}.3.(6)` and `8.4.2.9.(2)` records, with the 8.4.3.3 requirement carried only by the warning. The 6 actual changes are the D-02 no-LPD warning dropping its `8.4.3.1.(2)` half for `4.2.1.6.(1)(b)`; both D-22 economizer keep/strip decisions dropping `{economizer_article}` and retaining `5.2.2.7.(1)`; the D-20 air-economizer decision replacing `{prefix}.12. (Table -12 -> 5.2.2.8)` with `5.2.2.8.(1)` (the water-economizer `{prefix}.12. (Table -12 -> 5.2.2.9)` binding exists before and after Phase E and was never an 8.4-counted site); the D-85 orphan-VRF-removal `audit.info` replacing `8.4.4.1.` with `Table 5.2.12.1.-I` (the efficiency.py D-85 indeterminate-class warning cites that Table before and after); and the D-20 System 1 economizer record changing from `audit.info` to `audit.warn`.
